hypotheses.title: Coordinate prefill chunks across expert-parallel ranks using decode deadlines
hypotheses.mechanism: At each scheduling step, choose a graph-compatible prefill chunk using the earliest active decode deadline and a predicted iteration cost based on the slowest participating rank. Coordinate the choice across the expert-parallel group so one rank's prefill does not delay another rank's decode collective. This is an untested adaptation of deadline-aware chunking to the candidate DEP8 or DEP4 layouts.
hypotheses.nearest_prior_art: SLOWeave selects prefill chunks against decode deadlines; P-PAS adapts vLLM's token budget to prefill pressure. The earlier B200 decision already shortlisted a fixed DP-aligned prefill cadence.
hypotheses.new_adaptation: Use group-wide rank state and graph-compatible chunk choices, with explicit collective participation by idle ranks. A fixed cadence or direct paper port does not supply that coordinated decision.
hypotheses.code_surface: vLLM scheduler prefill budgeting, DP/EP rank coordination and iteration timing, compilation graph-bucket selection, and per-rank tracing. The resolved DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backend at the pinned image has not been established from the supplied sources.
hypotheses.online_policy: Observable state: active decode deadlines, queued prefill tokens, each participating rank's batch size and recent iteration time, plus available graph buckets. Decision: choose the largest compatible chunk whose predicted slowest-rank iteration meets the earliest deadline; require a minimum useful chunk and a bounded prediction margin. Action: schedule that chunk consistently across ranks. Overhead: rank-state exchange and prediction each iteration, with possible smaller GEMMs and extra launches. Fallback: the qualified fixed prefill interval and token budget when timing data is stale, coordination fails, or no chunk fits. Strongest static comparator: best measured fixed chunk/token budget and the recipe's fixed prefill interval at the same topology and concurrency.
hypotheses.strongest_objection: The workload may have too few simultaneous cache misses and decodes for chunk choice to matter. Existing fixed cadence and graph capture may already handle interference; per-step coordination could add synchronization and worsen TTFT or TPOT.

novelty.deployment: Untested on the specified B200 workload; active backend, DEP8/DEP4 configuration, and baseline inclusion are unknown.
novelty.implementation: The proposed group-wide deadline rule is distinct from the supplied fixed recipe and paper abstracts, but no source inspection establishes absence from the pinned implementation.
novelty.publication: Unestablished. SLOWeave, P-PAS, and earlier DP-cadence work substantially narrow the claim.

hypotheses.confidence: Moderate mechanism plausibility; low workload-specific benefit confidence.
hypotheses.readiness: Trace gate before implementation. No GPU result or bottleneck diagnosis is supplied.

experiment.control: Same pinned model, precision, requests, cache preparation, concurrency, eight-GPU budget, and active backend using the best qualified fixed chunk/token budget and recipe cadence. Evaluate DEP8 and two DEP4 only after each layout is independently configured and matched.
experiment.treatment: Group-coordinated deadline chunk policy with the same graph repertoire and memory budget.
experiment.measurements: Per-rank prefill/decode timing, collective wait, graph-bucket choice, queue age, cache misses, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, peak memory, and answer quality for approximately 8K/1K agent requests across load levels.
experiment.reject_if: No material mixed-step rank skew exists, prediction/coordination overhead consumes the available slack, or matched TTFT/TPOT/throughput and cost do not beat the strongest fixed setting.
experiment.correctness: Check unequal and empty rank batches, cancellation, cache hits and misses, graph replay, token ordering, and output agreement under identical precision and sampling.
experiment.cost: Trace and CPU replay before any proposed GPU experiment; actual build, capture, and runtime costs remain unknown.

hypotheses.revision_after_critique: Narrowed from generic adaptive prefill, already covered by SLOWeave and P-PAS, to collective-aware scheduling. Benefit is conditional on measured mixed-step rank skew.

hypotheses.title: Evict idle agent histories in bounded tail chunks
hypotheses.mechanism: Under KV pressure, rotate among idle agent trajectories and reclaim a bounded tail of each cached prefix while retaining its reusable beginning. Keep exact prefix-block ownership and all required hybrid-model state aligned. Returning agents recompute only the missing suffix. This is an untested adaptation to the target model's cache layout and DEP routing.
hypotheses.nearest_prior_art: RR-EVICT already uses round-robin tail eviction. CacheWise combines agent-aware scheduling and eviction in vLLM. A separate trace study reports that ordinary LRU remains strong for active sessions.
hypotheses.new_adaptation: Integrate tail eviction with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's actual cache-block and hybrid-state dependencies, and coordinate session placement when comparing DEP8 with two DEP4 replicas. The supplied evidence does not establish that this integration is absent or beneficial in the pinned backend.
hypotheses.code_surface: vLLM KV block manager and prefix index, session-to-prefix metadata, exact-token router affinity for two DEP4 engines, and hybrid-state invalidation/recompute path. The active backend and cache representation require source qualification.
hypotheses.online_policy: Observable state: free KV blocks, idle-session prefix trees, retained depth, prior reuse, session age, and per-engine placement. Decision: only below a memory watermark, rotate through idle sessions with reclaimable tails and remove a bounded suffix per pass while preserving a minimum exact reusable prefix; leave active requests intact. Action: release suffix blocks and invalidate dependent hybrid state atomically. Overhead: per-session bookkeeping, prefix-tree walks, and possible suffix recomputation. Fallback: existing LRU eviction or no special action when there is no pressure or no safe partial boundary. Strongest static comparator: current LRU plus a tuned fixed partial-eviction granularity at the same memory limit.
hypotheses.strongest_objection: The stated 75% cacheability is a target, not a measured hit rate or evidence of eviction pressure. Production-trace research finds little benefit from sophisticated replacement over LRU, and hybrid-state constraints may make safe tail reclamation expensive.

novelty.deployment: Unestablished for B200 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. No measured cache churn, avoidable misses, or per-engine locality is supplied.
novelty.implementation: RR-EVICT already implements the core policy in SGLang; novelty could only reside in a qualified vLLM/model-specific adaptation and is not established without source inspection.
novelty.publication: Unestablished; RR-EVICT and CacheWise are close prior art.

hypotheses.confidence: Moderate mechanism plausibility under sustained KV pressure; low benefit confidence for this workload.
hypotheses.readiness: Request-level cache trace and cache-layout correctness gate required before code work.

rubric.value: Potentially reduces returning-agent TTFT outliers if idle histories are evicted wholesale; extra recomputation and bookkeeping can raise cost.
rubric.mechanism: Concrete pressure-triggered, bounded, exact-prefix tail reclamation.
rubric.evidence: Close policy prior art and counterevidence are supplied; target workload cache pressure is unknown.
rubric.integration: High, due to hybrid state, cache-block ownership, and replica routing.
rubric.correctness: Never reuse partial or mismatched prefixes; invalidate all dependent state and compare outputs against uncached execution.
rubric.experiment: Trace gate, CPU eviction replay, then matched serving only if replay predicts avoidable recomputation.
rubric.cost: Trace/replay is cheaper than implementation; engineering and memory overhead are unknown. No GPU work performed.
rubric.distinctness: Distinct from the earlier one-use probationary admission idea and from router-only prefix placement.
rubric.research_contribution: Model-specific integration question; publication novelty unestablished.

experiment.control: Same engine layout, model precision, requests, routing, KV capacity, and cache preparation with current LRU; include fixed partial eviction and native CPU KV offload where applicable.
experiment.treatment: Bounded round-robin idle-history tail eviction with exact prefix and hybrid-state invalidation.
experiment.measurements: Per-request actual cache hits, evicted and recomputed blocks, session return gaps, KV occupancy, TTFT tail, TPOT, throughput, cost per token, peak memory, and output quality; report DEP8 and two DEP4 separately.
experiment.reject_if: The trace shows no meaningful idle-history eviction/recompute pattern, LRU or a fixed policy matches the replay, or matched serving increases tail latency or cost.
experiment.correctness: Test shared ancestors, concurrent descendants, partial blocks, cancellation, cross-engine routing, and each hybrid-state dependency against uncached outputs.
experiment.cost: CPU trace join and replay first; implementation, startup, and GPU experiment costs remain unknown.

hypotheses.revision_after_critique: Restricted to pressure-triggered idle-session tails and an explicit LRU comparator because the supplied trace study challenges elaborate eviction policies. No claim of benefit follows from the cacheability target.

comparators: Unchanged pinned vLLM and DeepSeek serving configuration, with resolved backend, MTP/DSpark state, precision, graph capture, and cache policy recorded before comparison.
